speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have experienced episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing. To help narrow this down, can you tell me if you lost consciousness completely during these episodes, and if anyone witnessed any specific movements or sounds?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Child Absence Epilepsy (Automatisms)

The detailed history of "staring" combined with specific automatisms like "hand gestures" and the muddy taste (likely post-ictal or auras) is highly suggestive of focal impaired awareness seizures, often misidentified as absence seizures in children. To confirm the etiology and localization of the seizure focus, I need to review the neurological findings. REQUEST TEST: EEG. REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage, as EEG is the diagnostic standard for seizure classification.
